Positioning remains notably low, with Rubner's informal indicator flagging skepticism from market participants questioning whether the rally can continue, he pointed out in a note. The S&P is up roughly 13% year-to-date even as market breadth wanes.
The concentration thesis is working precisely because the largest names are leading. Forty-five cents of every dollar flowing into the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust

Meanwhile, several catalysts are aligning for an "UpTober" scenario. Corporate buyback windows reopen in mid-October alongside Q3 earnings season—more than half of S&P 500 market-cap weight exits blackout by Nov. 1, nearly all of it by Nov. 8, with fresh authorizations arriving after a Q2 season that delivered roughly 33% EPS growth and the steepest positive revision path since at least 2000, Rubner said.
In addition, Streetwide estimates peg quarter-end pension rebalancing at north of $100B in equity sales versus bond purchases, pressure that is set to dissipate after Sept. 30.

Seasonality then flips bullish: Q4 of midterm years has averaged +5.6% from quarter-end versus +2.9% across all years. Rubner expects retail investors—sidelined during September's typical seasonal lull—to return for the year-end market rally.

title: Still on the sidelines? 'UpTober' might punish S&P 500 skeptics
